work_order.understanding:
Seven follow-ups from #67, all in two files. I re-checked each against the source and executed the plan for the whole of it in a scratch copy, so the CSS and the test code below are quoted from a run that passed, not from a reading.

(1) /approvals still overflows. .approval-actions was `display: flex` with no flex-wrap, so it defaulted to nowrap, and its <input> was `flex: 1` — grow 1, shrink 1, basis 0%. Shrinking cannot help: a flex item's automatic minimum is its content-based minimum, and an <input>'s is its intrinsic width (~234px in Chromium), which nothing in the file lowers. The row floors at 234+63+60+2x16 = 389px, .approval-card is a grid item in the display:grid .approval-list, the track sizes to that, and the page scrolls at 320/375/414 — 463 against all three, per QA. `overflow-wrap: anywhere` cannot touch it: it adds soft-wrap opportunities to text, and there is no text in that row that overflows. This is #48's defect one level down from the string. The fix is `min-width: 0` on the input (the declaration that actually lets the row shrink) plus `flex-wrap: wrap` on the row (which keeps both buttons reachable when that is still not enough); wrap alone does nothing while the input is floored at 234px.

(2) The pinned selector assertion was `selector.includes('.' + cls)`, a substring test over the rule's raw text, and it parsed `([^{}]+)` for the selector — which swallows a CSS comment, since a comment contains no braces. So prose naming a class satisfied the assertion, and .opportunity-roww satisfied it too. It now strips comments first, splits the selector group on commas, and compares the four compound selectors exactly.

(3) The "no later override" assertion was `assert.equal(wrapping.length, 1)`, which counts every rule in the file that mentions overflow-wrap. Appending `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` — a rule that cannot override a card rule — turned the suite red. It is now scoped to later rules whose selector actually names one of the four card classes.

(4) `.experiment-card *, .opportunity-row *, .approval-card *` are dead weight: overflow-wrap is inherited, so the three bare classes already cover every descendant.

(5) The comment above the rule was 21 lines in a file whose next-longest is 9, and two thirds of it was a record of rejected alternatives already in the work order and the assertion messages. It is now 8 lines.

(6) .tenant-name carried no wrap. The header name is `tenants.list()[0].name`, and src/api/routes.js:191 auto-creates an unknown tenant as `{ id: tenantId, name: tenantId }` — so the rendered name is the POST /v1/events body's tenant_id verbatim. .header-status is a flex row and the span's automatic minimum floors the header at the token: QA measured 1495px of scrollWidth at 320, 375 and 414. Latent on the seeded preview only because tenant_demo is created first.

(7) .learning-card is a fourth free-text card list outside .table-scroll that the enumeration missed. I rendered the seeded /opportunities: it carries `class="learning-card"` twice (the seed holds two accepted learnings) and `class="opportunity-row"`; /experiments carries `class="experiment-card"`. No rule in the stylesheet matched .learning-card.

On the rejection of v1: all three objections are addressed and each was fixed by execution, not by re-reading. (1) Both new test names are apostrophe-free and the file is `node --check` clean. (2) CARD_CLASSES is declared with the leading dot on all four entries, and I ran the full AC-7 matrix against the plan as now written: 66 pass / 0 fail unmutated, red for each of the seven mutations with messages naming the class or the declaration, and green for an appended `.page-footer` rule. (3) The render cross-check the v1 approach and tests[] promised but its test body omitted is now in the test: /experiments, /opportunities and /approvals are rendered and each of the four classes is required as a whole class token in the HTML of the route that renders it. I proved it bites by renaming `learning-card` to `learning-item` in src/web/pages.js alone, with the stylesheet untouched: the suite goes red on `the page still renders .learning-card as its own class`.

I could not re-measure layout in this sandbox — chromium is installed but does not start here — so the pixel numbers in the ticket are carried as given and the browser-visible claims are written as ACs for QA to measure on a real runner. Every layout claim is confirmed structurally in the CSS, and every test claim above was executed here.
work_order.root_cause: The card-name fix from #67 was expressed as an enumerated list of three class names plus a substring assertion over the stylesheet's text, so both halves are incomplete by construction: the enumeration missed a fourth free-text card list and the header, and the assertion could not tell a selector that matches a rendered element from one that matches nothing. A separate instance of the same family — a grid or flex item floored at its automatic minimum — survived at .approval-actions, one level below where #48 and #67 fixed it.
work_order.approach:
One stylesheet change covering the three live layout defects, one trim of the comment, and one rewrite of the pinned stylesheet assertion so it states the property it means and checks its class list against the markup the server actually renders.

CSS, in three places:
- The wrap rule becomes four bare classes — add `.learning-card`, delete the three `*` descendants (redundant: overflow-wrap is inherited), and replace the 21-line comment with 8 that state the defect, the grid-floor reason and the two constraints that must survive a future edit (scoped off the tables, `anywhere` not `break-word`).
- `.tenant-name` gains `min-width: 0` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, with three comment lines saying where the text comes from.
- `.approval-actions` gains `flex-wrap: wrap`, and `.approval-actions input` gains `min-width: 0` — the declaration that actually lets the row shrink below the input's 234px intrinsic minimum.

Test, in test/web/pages.test.js: rewrite the pinned assertion in the every-match style its neighbours already use, with the four changes findings 2, 3 and 5 ask for — strip comments before parsing, match compound selectors exactly rather than as substrings, scope the 'no later override' check to rules that touch the four card classes instead of counting every overflow-wrap rule in the file, and cross-check the rule's class list against the classes the server actually renders. The cross-check is four renders: /experiments for .experiment-card, /opportunities for .opportunity-row and .learning-card, and /approvals with a pending approval for .approval-card; each class is required as a whole whitespace-delimited token in that route's HTML, so a class renamed on the page fails the suite even though the stylesheet and the constant would both still say the old name. Add a `pendingApprovalRepos()` helper, because nothing in the product writes approval.requested and no test has ever rendered an approval card; without it both the cross-check and the /approvals layout are unverifiable here. Add two pins: the actions row (flex-wrap on the row, min-width on the input, plus a render that shows both have something to match) and the header tenant name (the wrap, plus a render of a 137-character tenant so the selector is known to match a real element).

files.why: Findings 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7. `overflow-wrap` is inherited, so the three `*` descendants state a property the bare classes already carry; `.learning-card` is a fourth free-text card list the enumeration missed; `.approval-actions` is a nowrap flex row whose <input> automatic minimum is its ~234px intrinsic width, which `overflow-wrap` cannot reach; and `.tenant-name` renders the request tenant_id verbatim into a flex row.

Findings 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. The pin the plan replaces asserted on a substring of the rule text (a renamed .opportunity-roww satisfied it) and counted every overflow-wrap rule in the file (an unrelated .page-footer rule failed it). The four class names are now compared as exact compound selectors and each one is required in the HTML of the route that renders it, so a selector that matches nothing in a real page fails the suite. pendingApprovalRepos() exists because nothing in the product writes approval.requested, so /approvals had never rendered a card in any test.

risks: Deleting the three `*` descendant selectors relies on overflow-wrap being inherited, which is true today and is the same fact #67's work order leaned on. If a future rule ever declares `overflow-wrap: normal` on an intermediate child, that descendant stops wrapping and the bare-class rule will not catch it, because it is not the kind of mistake the pinned assertion can see. No such rule exists in the file today.

The four class names are still a hand-maintained list, and the new cross-check narrows but does not close that. It catches a class renamed on the page and a class dropped from the rule, but it cannot catch a fifth free-text card list that nothing renders yet — a new `<li>` carrying free text outside .table-scroll needs its class added by hand, exactly as .learning-card did not get one.

Adding the wrap to .learning-card also reaches the metadata span under it (tier, confidence, evidence count, learning id), so a long learning id may now break mid-token inside the card. Cosmetic and inside a card, but it is a change no measurement in the ticket covers.

`min-width: 0` on the approval reason input lets it get narrower than its "Reason" placeholder at a 320px viewport, so the placeholder will clip while the field stays usable. Truncating the placeholder was rejected as a product-copy decision, not a layout one.

`flex-wrap: wrap` on .approval-actions means that at very narrow widths the Approve and Reject buttons drop onto a second line rather than beside the input. That is the intended behaviour and matches .journal-filters, but it is a visual change on a screen that had no rendered card in any earlier QA run, so there is no prior render to compare against.

The card-wrap pin now renders four routes, which makes the test slower and DB-touching where it was previously a pure file read. It is the only stylesheet pin in the file that touches storage, and that is deliberate: it is the half that makes the selector list a claim about the page rather than about the file.

The mutated-file checks in AC-7 and the rename check in AC-8 are run by hand against the working tree. Restore from git between each one; leaving a mutation in place is the obvious way to fail CI on the next run.
out_of_scope: `.awaiting-list li` on /journal?state=partial: it renders a generated decision_id and a formatted date, not user free text, so it gets no wrap. If a long decision id ever appears there it is its own ticket.

The client-rendered journal drawer body, which client.js fills from GET /v1/decisions/:id. It is a fixed-width overlay, not a server-rendered card list, and nothing in this ticket's measurements covers it.

`.checklist li` and the `.kpi-*` tiles: fixed product copy and formatted numbers, not free text. A blanket wrap would let a formatted money value break mid-digit, which is why it is not taken here either.

A blanket `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `#main`, or on every `ul`/`li` inside it. It would have found .learning-card and .tenant-name by itself, and it reaches .table-scroll cells and the monospace KPI values, which #67 measured undoing the table fix.

Writing an `approval.requested` event from the product — a write path, an executor call or a new seed row. Nothing creates one today, so the /approvals queue is empty in a running preview and this defect is latent. Making the queue non-empty changes what a first run shows and is a product decision the ticket does not ask for; the fix here makes the CSS correct for when one does, and the new test fixture makes it reachable for QA without one.
Truncating the tenant name with an ellipsis instead of wrapping it. The name is the only identifier the operator has for the account they are in, and the header has room to wrap onto a second line.
Any visual change to the 1100px layout. Every rule touched here applies at every width; the QA script sweeps 1100 and 1440 to confirm nothing moved, but no restyling is in scope.

alternatives_considered.approach: Scope the wrap by structure instead of by class name: `#main :not(.table-scroll *) { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }`
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It finds .learning-card and .tenant-name with no enumeration to keep up to date, which is closer to the actual root cause. But it also reaches every formatted money value and every monospace KPI number, so a long amount breaks mid-digit, and it is one edit away from re-reaching the table cells that #67 measured undoing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the three `*` descendant selectors and just add `.learning-card`
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: overflow-wrap is inherited, so the bare classes already cover every child; the descendants state the same property three more times, and they are what the new exact-compound assertion would have to pin forever. The reviewer measured the same result with them removed.

alternatives_considered.approach: `flex-wrap: wrap` on `.approval-actions` alone, without min-width: 0 on the input
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Wrapping the buttons does nothing while the input is floored at its ~234px intrinsic automatic minimum: the row is ~389px of min-content against ~208px of available width at a 320px viewport, and no line break is available inside a 234px-minimum item that also has to share the line. min-width: 0 is the declaration that does the work; the wrap is kept so the buttons stay reachable when even that is not enough.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the global `wrapping.length === 1` count and instead document that no other rule in the file may declare overflow-wrap
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It pins a property about the file rather than about the fix, so the first legitimate `.page-footer { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }` — a rule that cannot override the card rule — turns CI red. Reproduced in this run at 61 pass / 1 fail on the pre-change file. The message already states the narrower property; the assertion should be the message.

alternatives_considered.approach: Replace the stylesheet-text pin with a real layout assertion that measures scrollWidth in CI
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would be the strongest form, and the repo has no browser driver in CI and no appetite for a native-compiling dependency. The deliberate style of the existing pins in this file is a stylesheet-text assertion cross-checked against rendered markup, and that combination catches the exact class of mistake finding 2 describes — a selector that matches nothing in the page the server actually renders. AC-8 is the regression test for that half.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the cross-check the v1 approach and tests[] promised, and pin the four classes against the stylesheet only
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The reviewer offered this as the defensible second option and required the work order to pick one. The cross-check is taken: I built it, ran it, and proved it bites by renaming learning-card in pages.js alone and watching the suite go red. Keeping a claim in approach that the test body does not implement is what got v1 rejected.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete the pinned stylesheet test altogether, since findings 2 and 5 show it asserts the wrong things
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Those findings are defects of the assertions, not of pinning. The stylesheet is not observable from a rendered page and the browser check that would catch its regression is not in CI, so removing the pin leaves #67's fix unpinned with a green suite — the state finding 2 describes.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix the /approvals overflow by hiding the reason input at narrow widths rather than shrinking it
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It changes what the screen offers: an operator approving a spend at 320px would lose the reason field with no way to reach it, and no acceptance criterion or UI doc asks for that.

assumptions: The measurements in the issue body still hold. I re-derived each finding from the source and executed the whole plan in a scratch copy — 66/66 in the page suite, 306/306 in the full run, and the complete AC-7 and AC-8 mutation matrix — but chromium does not start in this sandbox, so the pixel numbers are carried forward rather than re-measured. AC-1 through AC-6 are for QA to measure on a real runner.
`overflow-wrap` is an inherited property, so a bare class on a card reaches every descendant. The stylesheet already relies on this in the `#main > *` comment.

Nothing in the product writes `approval.requested` today (one hit, the read at src/web/pages.js:924), so the /approvals card is reachable in a test only through the repository layer. The seeded /opportunities renders `.learning-card` and `.opportunity-row` and the seeded /experiments renders `.experiment-card`, so the cross-check passes on a plain seed with no fixture. I enumerated the class attributes of both renders to confirm this rather than assuming it.
unknowns: Whether the operator would rather see a long tenant name truncated than wrapped to a second header line. Wrapping is what every other free-text surface in this app does, and the header region is a flex row that already wraps, so this follows the existing pattern rather than deciding a new one — but it is the one place in this change a person might have wanted a different answer.

Whether the reviewer's 422px /approvals track matches this runner's Chromium. The fix is structural and does not depend on the exact number, but AC-1 states the before and after so a mismatch is visible rather than silent.

I applied all three files[] changes to a scratch copy of the repo and ran them — test/web/pages.test.js goes 64/0 before and 66/0 after, the full `node --test` run is 306 pass / 0 fail, and `node --check` confirms the new test file parses. All three of the reviewer's objections are answered by that run, including the two the reviewer identified as non-discriminating (the missing leading dot, which made AC-7 inert, and the absent render cross-check, which is now proven to bite by renaming learning-card in pages.js alone). The six browser criteria that rest on those numbers are written with their pre-change baselines quoted, which is where the remaining uncertainty sits. review.title: The new header pin cannot tell a selector that matches a rendered element from one that matches nothing — the exact blind spot finding 2 names, reproduced in the sibling test this same PR adds. The card-wrap test was rewritten to close it; the tenant-name test was not. It asserts the CSS declares `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on `.tenant-name` and that the *testid* element renders the whole name, but it never asserts that `class="tenant-name"` is on that element, so deleting the class from pages.js leaves the suite fully green while the whole rule pins a selector that matches nothing in the page. The work order's approach says the render is "what makes the selector a fact about the page"; for the header it does not.

`test/web/pages.test.js:1532`

Evidence: Scratch copy at /tmp/p71 on sdlc/issue-71. Baseline: `# pass 66 # fail 0`. Then in src/web/pages.js:73 the opening tag `<span class="tenant-name" id="tenant-name" data-testid="tenant-name">` was replaced with `<span id="tenant-name" data-testid="tenant-name">` (class attribute removed, stylesheet untouched) and `node --test test/web/pages.test.js` was re-run: `# pass 66 # fail 0`. The `data-testid` is the only hook the assertion at test/web/pages.test.js:1532 reads, and `.tenant-name` is a bare class selector with no fallback. Compare the sibling tests, which do close it: the approval test asserts `/<li class="approval-card">/` and `/<form class="approval-actions"/` in the markup, and the card-wrap test requires each of the four classes as a whole class token.

Fix: Tie the class to the element in the render the test already performs, the way the other two new tests do. After the `shown` assertion, add something like `assert.match(html, /<span class="tenant-name"[^>]*data-testid="tenant-name">/, 'the element the rule targets is the one the header renders, so the selector has something to match');` — or fold the class into the existing exec by matching `<span class="tenant-name"[^>]*data-testid="tenant-name">([^<]*)</`.

review.title: The rewritten "no later override" check is blind to an override nested inside an at-rule, because the rule parser `([^{}]+)\{([^}]*)\}` cannot balance braces. The check is correctly scoped to selectors naming a card class (the .page-footer negative case is fixed and verified), but every other responsive edit in this stylesheet is an `@media` block, and a card-class override written that way is missed — including at exactly the ≤900px widths this ticket exists to fix. Today the loop is also vacuous: only two rules in src/web/styles.css declare overflow-wrap and both sit before the card rule, so the loop body never executes on the shipped file.

`min-width: 0` on `.tenant-name` is inert, is the one declaration in this diff that the new comment above the rule does not mention, and is the one declaration the header test does not pin — its load-bearing twin on `.approval-actions input` has both. Either drop it or say why it is there and pin it.
review.detail:
`min-width: 0` on `.tenant-name` is inert, is the one declaration in this diff that the new comment above the rule does not mention, and is the one declaration the header test does not pin — its load-bearing twin on `.approval-actions input` has both. Either drop it or say why it is there and pin it.

`src/web/styles.css:108`

Evidence: Measured in headless Chromium at a 320px viewport against the 137-character tenant of AC-2, the branch's own stylesheet applied. As shipped, `.tenant-name` computes to `min-width: 0px; overflow-wrap: anywhere` and the document reads scrollWidth 320 against innerWidth 320, the span 272px wide over 6 lines. Overriding just `min-width` back to `auto` at runtime: scrollWidth still 320 against 320, span still 272px. Overriding `overflow-wrap` to `normal` as well: the document goes to 1495px wide, matching the QA number quoted in the issue and the work order exactly. So the wrap alone carries the whole fix and `min-width: 0` changes nothing — which is the same fact the file's own comment states three rules above, where it picks `anywhere` over `break-word` because only `anywhere` collapses intrinsic sizing. Contrast `.approval-actions input` (src/web/styles.css:397), where `min-width: 0` is demonstrably load-bearing: reverting it at runtime, with `flex-wrap: wrap` still in place, takes /approvals from scrollWidth 320 back to 463 at a 320px viewport. That is why the sibling comment explains both of its declarations and the header comment explains only the wrap.

Fix: Delete `min-width: 0` from `.tenant-name` — the wrap is the whole fix and one less declaration is one less thing to re-derive. If it is kept deliberately as belt-and-braces, add it to the three lines of comment above the rule with the reason, and extend the header test's every-match pin the way the approval test pins its input, so a future edit cannot remove it silently.

The card-wrap test renders `/opportunities` twice with the same repositories, producing the same HTML twice. One render serves both keys.

`test/web/pages.test.js:1468`

Evidence: test/web/pages.test.js:1467 and :1468 are byte-identical calls, `await renderPage('/opportunities', { repositories: seeded })`, differing only in the key they are stored under; `seeded` is a single `seededRepos('pages-card-wrap-')` from line 1465. The loop below iterates `CARD_CLASSES` and looks each class up in `markup`, so the second string is the first one verbatim. This is the one redundancy in a test the work order's own risk list flags as newly expensive — 'the card-wrap pin now renders four routes, which makes the test slower and DB-touching where it was previously a pure file read' — where three renders would do the same work.

qa.title: The journal decision drawer scrolls stored free text sideways instead of wrapping it, unlike the four card lists this PR fixed
qa.expected: Free text that is one unbreakable token wraps inside the surface that shows it, which is the rule this PR applies to .experiment-card, .opportunity-row, .approval-card and .learning-card.
qa.actual: With a decision carrying 120-character unbreakable evidence_refs, memory_refs, policy_decision_id and worst_reasonable_case, the drawer body lays out 1870px of content inside 271px (320), 326px (375) and 365px (414) of client width, and 6-7 elements sit at right=1895.3, past the viewport edge. The page does not widen only because #journal-drawer is position: fixed and therefore excluded from document scroll width; the text is reachable by scrolling the drawer horizontally, which its `overflow-y: auto` makes `overflow-x: auto`.
repro: Create a decision for tenant_demo whose record carries 120-character unbreakable evidence_refs, memory_refs, policy_decision_id and worst_reasonable_case (repositories.decisions.create)
Click the row's open-decision action for that decision
qa.suspected_cause: The wrap rule is scoped to four list classes and the drawer body is not one of them. This is the scoping trade the PR's own comment makes -- "Scoped to these four lists, never to #main" -- and #journal-drawer-body renders the same kind of stored free text by a different route (client-rendered from GET /v1/decisions/:id). Nothing in this diff touches the drawer, so this predates #71 and is filed rather than fixed here.

qa.title: Tab escapes the journal decision dialog on the first press, while the dialog is marked aria-modal
qa.expected: A dialog rendered with role="dialog" aria-modal="true" holds focus, or traps it, so a keyboard user is not delivered to page content sitting behind an overlay that claims the rest is unavailable.
qa.actual: On opening a decision the Close button is focused, and the first Tab lands on the skip link outside #journal-drawer, then walks the brand and the five nav links behind it. The drawer is fixed and covers the whole viewport at this width, so the focus ring is drawn on content the user cannot see. #journal-drawer carries no tabindex, so the drawer itself is not a tab stop.
repro: Open /journal at a viewport 900px wide or narrower
Observe focus move to the skip link outside the dialog, which is aria-modal="true"
qa.suspected_cause: src/web/client.js focuses the Close button on open but installs no keydown handler for Tab, so the dialog is announced as modal and behaves as a plain panel. The file's own comment on the error panel shows the focus-on-open pattern is deliberate; the trap is the part that is missing. The contrast with .table-scroll, which the stylesheet gives tabindex="0" precisely so its overflow is keyboard-scrollable, is the closest thing to a precedent in this codebase. Predates #71 -- nothing in this diff touches the drawer.
